column3: Close to the Greek; “garden plants” is rendered “herbs” and “perching” as “nest.”
NKJV names “Jesus,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text has “He went into the house.”
Close to the Greek; “consummation” is rendered “end.”
NKJV reads “this age,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text has “the age.”
Close to the Greek; “causes of sin” is rendered “things that offend.”
Close to the Greek; “weeping” is rendered “wailing.”
NKJV has “ears to hear,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text has only “ears.”
NKJV begins with “Again,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text has no “again” here.
Close to the Greek; “weeping” is rendered “wailing.”
NKJV includes “Jesus said to them” and “Lord,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text has only the question and the answer “Yes.”
Close to the Greek; “miraculous powers” is rendered “mighty works.”
NKJV reads “Joses,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text reads “Joseph.”
